## THE MILESTONE-CENTERPIECE — vox-018's PASS/MISS Definition

`sprint-08.md` names vox-018 as M01's "one unretired unknown." Its own Acceptance Criteria say the
verdict must be rendered "honestly" but do not define the statistic, the window, or the culling-proof
method precisely enough to prevent a favorable misread. This plan defines all three, binding on the
evidence doc. **These definitions are QA-authored (per this sprint's Key Content directive), not
copied from the story file** — flagged as such, not silently presented as story-original.

### What "60 FPS sustained" means (the gating statistic)

- **Gating statistic: p95 frame time ≤ 16.6 ms** (equivalently, p95 instantaneous FPS ≥ 60), not the
  average. Average FPS is recorded alongside for context but is explicitly **not** sufficient alone —
  an average can hide a chronic tail of dips that "feels" fine in a single-number summary. This
  mirrors the project's own existing precedent: ADR-0008's spike used p95 (16.7 ms at 3x), not avg,
  as its pass/fail bar; this plan applies the same discipline to rendering.
- **Duration/window: a continuous windowed capture of at least 60 real seconds, or at least 3 full
  camera sweeps across the production-scale view window (`view_radius_chunks = 24`, the shipped
  config default) — whichever is longer.** A single short burst is not sufficient; the raw log must
  contain a real per-frame or per-second time series long enough to compute a meaningful p95, not a
  handful of samples. (This duration is a QA-defined floor — the story itself does not specify one.)
- **Max/worst single frame** is recorded but does not by itself cause a MISS, unless a later smoke
  run shows the same worst-case pattern recurring on consecutive frames (the direct analog of
  Call-out 4's re-tune escalation clause, applied to rendering hitches from streaming stalls).
- **Draw calls ≤ 2000 is a HARD per-sample ceiling**, checked at every sampled frame across the whole
  capture window — not an average. This is an architecture budget (`technical-preferences.md`), not
  a soft target; one frame over 2000 is a MISS on that axis regardless of the FPS numbers.

### How culling-ON is PROVEN, not asserted

A measured 60 FPS with culling silently disabled is a false PASS — this is the exact failure mode
ADR-0014 names as "expired mitigation." Proof requires **both**:
1. **Grep-guard, re-run fresh for this story** (not assumed still-true from vox-007's S6 evidence):
   zero `CULL_DISABLED` in `src/voxel_world/` and the terrain shader — extend/re-run
   `mesher_material_contract_test.gd`'s existing assertion as part of THIS story's own evidence, not
   cited by reference to a prior sprint's pass.
2. **A visual proof in the SAME measurement session** — at least one PNG from a grazing/low-oblique
   angle at production scale, mirroring vox-007's own "historically riskiest angle" methodology
   (`vox-007-terrain-20260724-2.png`'s precedent): side/cliff faces must render solidly with the
   culling material's `cull_back` mode genuinely active. The FPS/draw-call numbers and the
   culling-is-genuinely-on screenshot must come from the **same** windowed run, not a separate
   one-off check — a PASS on FPS from one session and a culling-proof screenshot from another would
   not actually prove the two facts held simultaneously.

### PASS / MISS verdict logic

**PASS** requires ALL of: (1) p95 frame time ≤ 16.6 ms over the ≥60s/≥3-sweep window, (2) draw calls
≤ 2000 at every sampled frame, (3) culling proven ON per both checks above, (4) the measurement is
genuinely windowed on a real GPU (headless does not count — this is unenforceable by grep, so the
evidence doc's stated launch command and hardware class are the audit trail). On PASS: criterion #12
closes, culling stays enabled, headroom recorded.

**MISS** on ANY of the four: record the shortfall precisely (which statistic missed, by how much),
file the named remediation stories (greedy meshing — ADR-0014's named reserve — and/or
`visibility_range_end` tightening and/or a further build/unload budget re-tune, per the story's own
Implementation Notes), and **criterion #12 stays OPEN** — recorded explicitly as open at hand-off, not
silently implied fixed by the sprint closing. **No `CULL_DISABLED` fallback under any circumstance,
including a razor-thin miss** — the story's own Forbidden list and this plan agree exactly here.

### Open question this plan surfaces, does not resolve

**"Mid-range PC target" has no defined spec sheet anywhere in this project** (grep of
`technical-preferences.md`, the milestone doc, and `docs/` found only the label, never a CPU/GPU/RAM
baseline). The evidence doc's "hardware class" field is therefore unverifiable against any
project-defined baseline — a PASS measured on a high-end dev machine would not actually prove the
mid-range target holds. **Recommend producer/technical-director define a minimum-spec reference
(even a rough one) before or alongside this measurement** — this plan cannot manufacture that
baseline unilaterally. Until it exists, record the actual test machine's real specs verbatim in the
evidence doc and flag the gap explicitly rather than implying "mid-range" was verified.

### vox-018 — Live Valley wiring + 60-FPS-with-culling measurement — Integration + Advisory-Perf
**Test file path (BLOCKING half)**: `neues-spiel/tests/integration/voxel_world/live_view_window_wiring_test.gd`
**Evidence path (Advisory half, informs #12's closure)**: `production/qa/evidence/voxel-world-60fps-culling-evidence-20260725.md`

**What the BLOCKING integration test covers**:
- AC-1: `VoxelWorldMeshStreamer` hosted under `Valley`; `update_view_window()` invoked every
  `_process` frame with the live `CameraInput` focus cell; `build_initial_window()` invoked exactly
  once at boot; streamer `setup()` reached ONLY via GameWorld's injected-tier path (ADR-0005) — assert
  no second call site.
- AC-2: a world larger than the view window, focus swept across it — meshed-chunk membership and
  draw-call count track the window, not world size; draw calls stay ≤ 2000 headless (a coarse
  correctness check; the real FPS number is the windowed measurement below, not this test).

above for the full PASS/MISS definition. Do not substitute a headless number for this — headless
cannot render a viewport texture (GdUnit4 cannot produce this evidence; the windowed tool-scene
precedent, `mesher_evidence`/`camera_sandbox`, is mandatory).

**Edge cases to cover (integration test)**:

- Re-confirm `mesher_material_contract_test.gd`'s `CULL_DISABLED` grep-guard still returns zero
  matches as part of this story's own test run (Call-out re: culling proof above), not cited from S6.

### villager-ai-022 — Per-tick re-tune, Deciding-budget half + `decision_interval` — Config/Data
**Verified via**: smoke check + a re-run performance suite, per its own Story Type — but this plan
adds two BLOCKING measurement assertions beyond a bare smoke pass, per the sprint's Key Content
directive.

**What to verify**:
- `max_deciding_per_tick` 1→5 AND `decision_interval` 2→4 recorded as the SAME coordinated change as
  tick-007 (shared rationale, quick-spec).
- **Story-025 stress harness RE-RUN at the new defaults (quick-spec AC1/AC2/AC3), with a
  before/after comparison table against the Sprint 7 baseline recorded in
  `production/qa/evidence/villager-ai-stress-evidence-retune-20260725.md`** — replacing the
  quick-spec's [ESTIMATED] ~5.47 ms per-tick figure with a measured one, in both directions (record
  the delta whichever way it falls, per the quick-spec's own AC2 wording).
  - Measured worst-case ticks-to-decide at pop 30, synchronized mass-Deciding (Scenario 3) is ≤ 6
    ticks (matching `wait_ticks_max` at K=5).
  - Queue-depth sample at pop 30 shows quiescence between periodic-recheck cycles — measurably below
    the S7 chronic ~29.5/30 average, not merely "still bounded."
  - Frame budget holds at both 1x and 3x warp at pop 30 with the new values.
- **Determinism regression, BLOCKING (ADR-0009, quick-spec AC5)**: the same synchronized-mass-Deciding
  scenario run twice at the new values produces an identical dequeue order both runs. This is not new
  work — the existing determinism harness is re-run against the new config, not re-authored.
- **Burst-frame amplification, BLOCKING per Call-out 4**: the stress harness (or a dedicated case
  within it) drives an explicit 12-tick catch-up frame at `max_deciding_per_tick=5` (i.e., a
  post-stall resume) and **measures** the actual one-off frame cost against the quick-spec's ~37ms
  estimate — turning an "accepted, estimated" tradeoff into a measured one, consistent with how every
  other figure in this re-tune is being upgraded from estimated to measured this sprint. The test
  must additionally assert this pattern is observed as a single, isolated frame event within the
  stress run — not recurring on consecutive frames (the quick-spec's own escalation trigger for
  further profiling). If the harness cannot practically simulate a stall this sprint, the evidence
  doc must say so explicitly and carry the ~37ms figure forward as still-estimated, not silently
  omit the check.
- **No FSM/staggering code changes** — grep/diff confirms this is a pure config value change (both
  stories' own explicit constraint).

**Edge cases to cover**:
- Warp-invariance and pause-tolerance of the existing tick/pause test suite are RE-RUN (not assumed
  passing) against the new `max_ticks_per_frame=12`/`max_deciding_per_tick=5` pair — see Smoke Test
  Scope item 2 for the explicit re-run requirement.

  `unstuck_watchdog_threshold_ticks` teleports to the F5 rescue cell, releases any held claim, and
  fires `villager_unstuck` with incremented per-villager AND world-total counters.
- AC52: a held claim releases exactly once (no double-release, no orphan); no held claim (e.g.
  traveling to a bed) has zero claim-release side effect and bed ownership is unaffected.
- AC32: Idle/Wandering/Sleeping/Breather villagers with no legal step stay put with the distress flag
  set and NEVER teleport — the explicit scope-boundary complement.
- The rescue sets `current_cell` atomically at a tick boundary and snaps `_visual_position` (no
  lerp) — grep/assert the rescue code path never interpolates.
- `stuck_tick_count` resets to 0 the instant relief is available; a villager is rescued only once
  per stuck episode.

**Binding new assertion (Call-out re: watchdog vs. Deciding scheduler, "no double-decide")**:
- **After a rescue, the villager re-enters Deciding through the SAME FIFO-queue + `max_deciding_per_tick`
  budget path every other Deciding entry uses — it must not be granted a bonus immediate decide that
  bypasses the budget, and it must not be double-enqueued if it was already waiting in the Deciding
  queue at the moment it was rescued.** Assert: (a) a rescued villager's post-rescue Deciding pass
  consumes one of the tick's `max_deciding_per_tick` budget slots like any other entry, never an
  extra unbudgeted slot; (b) if the villager happened to already hold a queued Deciding-request at
  rescue time, the rescue does not create a second, duplicate queue entry for the same villager. This
  is a QA-defined assertion (not named in either story's own Test Evidence) — it is the concrete,
  testable form of the sprint's "watchdog must not fight the deciding scheduler" directive.

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7 (existing ACs) + ~2 (the new scheduler-interaction assertion).

### villager-ai-016 — Seal-prevention negative-write gate & livelock escape (F6) — Logic + Integration (Call-out 1)
**Test file paths (BOTH BLOCKING)**:
- `neues-spiel/tests/unit/villager_ai/seal_prevention_test.gd` (story's own header requirement)
- `neues-spiel/tests/integration/villager_ai/seal_prevention_real_build_write_test.gd` (this plan's
  addition, Call-out 1)

**What the unit test covers**:
- AC54: a build-job completion that would leave the builder with zero legal steps is refused, the
  claim releases back to the queue, and `abandon_count` for that (job, villager) pair increments by 1.
- AC55: a dig/demolition completion that would trap the builder proceeds unconditionally — dig/
  demolition never trigger seal-prevention refusal.
- AC56: the same (job, villager) pair refused `seal_prevention_abandon_limit` times → the next attempt
  writes unconditionally regardless of the trap check (livelock escape; the builder is left sealed
  for the watchdog to rescue).
- `abandon_count` resets when the job is claimed by a DIFFERENT villager; monotonic bound otherwise.
- `_visual_position` is never read by `would_trap_builder` (grep/assert discrete `current_cell`/
  body-column only, per the control-manifest's absolute rule).

**What the integration test covers (the real-build-loop requirement, Call-out 1)**:
- Drive a villager through the REAL claim→travel→on-site→completion cycle (the same real components
  villager-ai-012's S7 crown assembled — real `CommitPipeline`, real `ConstructionTickLoop`, real
  claim/queue), constructed so the builder's OWN completing cell is its last legal exit — i.e., a
  genuine self-seal scenario driven through the real write call site the Building System actually
  uses at tick-boundary completion, not a mocked `would_trap_builder(...)` unit call.
- Assert the real write is refused/requeued (or, at the abandon-limit boundary, proceeds and the real
  watchdog rescues it) exactly as the unit test's boundary logic predicts — proving the gate is wired
  into the ACTUAL write call site, not merely correct in isolation. This is the "a villager may not
  build themselves into a sealed pocket, tested against real construction writes" requirement named
  in this sprint's Key Content directive.
- Cross-check AC55's dig/demolition exemption against the real demolition write path too, not only
  the build-completion path, since ADR-0016 makes demolition job-based and uniform with construction.

**Estimated test count**: ~6-7 (unit) + ~3-4 (integration).

## Smoke Test Scope

**Baseline**: 843 blocking + 5 advisory perf tests (Sprint 7 actuals, "green with 0 orphans on every
story commit").

**What Sprint 8 adds**: up to 10 new/extended test files across the 10 Must stories (vox-018's
integration half, building-024/025/026/027, villager-ai-014/015/016 ×2 files) summing to roughly
**~40-48 new BLOCKING tests** (vox-018 ~5-6, building-024 ~5-6, building-025 ~4-5, building-026 ~4-5,
building-027 ~3-4, villager-ai-014 ~7-9 across two files, villager-ai-015 ~8-9, villager-ai-016 ~9-11
across two files) plus tick-007/villager-ai-022's smoke-verified re-tune (no new automated test count,
but a re-run of the existing determinism/warp/pause suites, see item 2) plus **~4-6 more if both
Nice items land** (vox-016 smoke-only, vox-017 ~4-5). Target regression count at sprint close:
**~883-891** (committed-only) or **~887-897** (+both Nice) — zero failures, zero errors, zero skipped
on every BLOCKING file.

1. **Full regression suite runs green**: all 843 existing tests PLUS every new/extended Sprint-8 test
   file — 843 is a floor, not a ceiling. **Fail-fast-per-suite note (carried from S6/S7 actuals)**:
   the GdUnit CLI runner halts a suite's remaining cases on its first failing assertion — run each new
   suite individually at least once during development so a later assertion's failure is not masked.

2. **Re-tune regression re-run — named explicitly, not assumed still-true**: every existing tick/pause/
   warp test (the pre-existing pause-freezes-`game_delta`, warp-multiplier, and determinism suites
   from the Time & Tick and Villager AI epics) is RE-RUN against `max_ticks_per_frame=12`,
   `max_deciding_per_tick=5`, `decision_interval=4` — not assumed unaffected because the change is
   "config-only." A config-only change can still break a test that hardcodes an assumption about the
   old cadence (e.g., a test asserting `decision_interval`'s old 0.5s real-time meaning would now be
   silently wrong at 1.0s). Confirm: (a) pause still freezes `game_delta` and Deciding activity
   identically; (b) warp multiplier (1x/2x/3x) still scales tick cadence correctly at the new budget;
   (c) the mass-Deciding determinism suite (ADR-0009) produces an identical dequeue order run-to-run
   at the new values (quick-spec AC5).

3. **The anti-stuck chain's real-write seal-prevention test is smoke item #1 — this sprint's headline
   gate (mirrors S7's crown-is-item-#1 discipline):**
   - `tests/integration/villager_ai/seal_prevention_real_build_write_test.gd` runs headless and green,
     proving the negative-write gate against the REAL Building System completion write — a
     half-failure (unit passes, integration fails, or vice versa) must be visible as two distinct
     red lines, not folded into one pass/fail summary.
   - `tests/unit/villager_ai/unstuck_watchdog_test.gd`'s new scheduler-interaction assertions (no
     double-decide, no bonus budget slot) pass.
   - `tests/unit/villager_ai/rescue_target_bfs_test.gd` + the AC53 integration fixture both pass.
   - Re-run at smoke/hand-off time even if they passed at story-completion time — the anti-stuck
     chain is serial-depth-3 and each story consumes the previous one's real output, making a
     late-landing wiring break the specific risk this smoke item guards against.

4. **Building-tool grep-guard family (Call-out 3, new this sprint)**:
   - `rg --glob "*.gd" "BlueprintCell\.new\(" src/building_system/` — every match must resolve to
     `commit_pipeline.gd` itself; zero matches in `wall_tool.gd`/`floor_tool.gd`/`roof_tool.gd`/
     `block_tool.gd` (or whatever their final filenames are).
   - `rg --glob "*.gd" "voxel_world\.(set_cell|bulk_write|clear_cell)" src/building_system/` — zero
     matches outside the pipeline/tick-loop's own established write call sites (unchanged from S5/S6
     precedent, now re-checked against four new tool files).

5. **vox-018's PASS/MISS verdict is rendered and recorded — smoke item #2**:
   - The evidence doc exists, states the verdict per this plan's definition, and (on MISS) names
     remediation stories. A smoke run that is silent on this is itself a smoke-check failure to
     surface, per this sprint's Key Content directive ("MISS stays OPEN, no CULL_DISABLED fallback").
   - `CULL_DISABLED` grep-guard (carried, re-checked): zero matches, confirmed fresh this sprint (not
     cited from S6/S7).

6. **Nav-race / forbidden-pattern families — carried forward, re-checked against this sprint's new
   surface area (rescue teleport, seal-write gate, drawing-tool commit paths)**:
   - Zero `NavigationServer3D`/`NavigationAgent3D`/`NavigationRegion3D` in Villager AI/Build Validation.
   - Zero `Thread`/`WorkerThreadPool` in Villager AI (voxel residency's own `WorkerThreadPool` usage,
     ADR-0015, is out of this grep's scope by design).
   - `rg --glob "*.gd" "SceneTree\.paused|Engine\.time_scale"` across `neues-spiel/` — zero matches.
   - `_visual_position` never read outside the movement/rendering path — re-checked specifically
     against villager-ai-015's rescue snap and villager-ai-016's `would_trap_builder` (both read
     discrete `current_cell`/body-column only, never `_visual_position`).

7. **No synchronous I/O / no time-scale coupling — carried from ADR-0015, re-checked because vox-018

   falls back to a synchronous read/gen on the render thread.

8. **CW-winding/culling regression (carried, folded into item 5 above for this sprint specifically

    smoke process itself). Do not treat "exit 0" alone as sufficient; the orphan count must also read

- [ ] All acceptance criteria verified via passing automated test or smoke-measurement result, by
      declared Type: **2 Config/Data** stories (tick-007, villager-ai-022, +Nice vox-016 if pulled);
      **5 Logic** stories (building-024/025/026/027, villager-ai-014); **2 Logic-with-mandatory-
      Integration** stories (villager-ai-015's own Logic evidence, villager-ai-016's Logic+Integration
      pair per Call-out 1); **2 Integration** stories (vox-018's wiring half, +Nice vox-017 if pulled)
      — **1 Advisory-Performance** measurement (vox-018's FPS/culling verdict, never a Done blocker
      for any OTHER story, but BLOCKING for criterion #12's own closure specifically)
